articles.title: China’s central bank goes daily on 1.25% overnight repo, moving to Fed-style anchor
articles.expand: For China’s money markets, daily fixed-rate overnight operations should mean tighter control of short-term funding costs and less of the month-end and tax-season volatility that has periodically rattled interbank rates. The shift also changes what traders will watch: the overnight rate, not the seven-day rate, now looks set to become the signal of PBOC intent, so any future adjustment to the 1.25% level will be read as a policy move. Stronger input inflation linked partly to oil, together with hiring close to its fastest pace in years and rising backlogs, points to a tight goods sector rather than a weakening one. For the yen, the data lean modestly supportive if they reinforce expectations of tighter policy.
